blindSummary:
Three trans women were murdered in less than a week in July 2024; five transfeminicides were recorded for the year, second only to the country's highest-count state/province. Activists reported six killed in a short period and accused three levels of government of rights omissions. The state/province's penal code contains no transfeminicide offence, and its 2019 hate-crime provision covers sexual orientation but not gender identity — meaning a visitor assaulted in its largest city faces a legal framework with no specific protective category.

Legislative response has been refusal: an initiative filed by a local trans collective was 'ignored and finally lapsed,' prompting a 50+-day protest encampment outside the state/province congress still ongoing in January 2026. A deputy of a smaller party in 2026 could only ask the congress to 'unfreeze' the bill. There is no investigative unit, no protocol, and no named offence to invoke.

Well below the national average. Compared with the leading state/province, which pairs similar lethality with a dedicated investigation unit, mandatory-response protocols and a gender police force, this state/province's absence of any transfeminicide offence or investigative machinery is the decisive divergence. And compared with the state/province that was first in the country to typify the crime, in 2024, this state/province's explicit legislative refusal is the opposite signal.
